# Changelog

All notable changes to the "Isocenter" project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Breaking

- **BREAKING: the basic profile is Table E.1-1 of DICOM PS3.15 Annex E (2026c), row by row, not a 35-tag subset of it (#547).** 0.9.7's `BASIC_PROFILE` covered 35 of the table's 656 rows, commented "Reduced for common usage", so identifiers the table names reached every export. Measured on 0.9.7 with pydicom's `CT_small.dcm` carrying one identifier of each kind: 25 of 26 survived a bare-session `anonymize()` and export. They included Instance Creation Date and Time, Admitting Date, Last Menstrual Date, Mother's Birth Name, Telephone Numbers, Physician(s) of Record, Requesting Physician, Device Serial Number, Protocol Name, Study Comments, a Request Attributes Sequence carrying Requested Procedure and Scheduled Procedure Step IDs, a Content Sequence carrying a Person Name, and Overlay Comments. The profile now has **620 rules** (466 `REMOVE`, 154 `EMPTY`), derived row by row: against 0.9.7, 555 rows gained a rule, 13 changed action, 17 matched, 5 departures were kept, 66 rows deliberately have no rule, and no rule names a tag the table does not. `tests/fixtures/ps3.15-2026c-table-e1-1.json` is the table, `tests/support/annex_e.py` says how each code becomes an action and names every departure with its reason, and `tests/test_basic_profile_annex_e.py` holds the literal in `profiles.py` equal to that derivation. `FLOOR_POLICY` is also 620: Patient's Age is now a basic rule, so all three research defaults override one.
  - **What the old profile got wrong besides coverage.** It removed four attributes that are Type 2 in the Patient and General Study modules -- Accession Number, Referring Physician's Name, Study ID and Patient's Birth Date -- so every export was missing required elements, and `IODValidator`, which does not check them, said nothing. This is 0.9.6's Study Time defect (#503) at four more tags. Every code that allows zero length (`Z`, `X/Z`, `Z/D`, `X/Z/D`) now empties the attribute instead of removing it: zero length is valid wherever the table's `X` is valid (Type 3) and wherever its `Z` is (Type 2), and removal is valid only for Type 3. Thirteen 0.9.7 rules change from `REMOVE` to `EMPTY`: Patient's Birth Date, Patient's Sex, Acquisition Date, Time and DateTime, Content Date and Time, Accession Number, Referring Physician's Name, Study ID, Institution Name, Station Name and Operators' Name. `X` and `X/D` remove.
  - **A rule on a sequence now does something.** `PhiInspector._scan_instance` looked a configured tag up only among each item's attributes, so a `REMOVE` or `EMPTY` on a sequence tag raised no finding, the instance read clear, and the sequence was exported with its items (measured: Request Attributes Sequence under `REMOVE`, Referenced Study Sequence under `EMPTY`). That was true of every user rule on a sequence before this release, and would have been of 56 of the new basic rules. `REMOVE` now deletes the sequence and `EMPTY` leaves it present with zero items; both are applied innermost first, as private sequences are (#167), and the deepest-first order now holds with `remove_private_tags: false` too. `REPLACE`, `SHIFT` and `JITTER` on a sequence did nothing before and still do nothing, but now log one warning per tag and action. A private sequence named in `phi_tags` is still raised once.
  - **What a previously-working session now does differently.** Every session that applies a policy -- a bare `Session`, `privacy_profile: basic`, or a config with no `privacy_profile` line -- exports different files. `privacy_profile: none` and an external profile file are unchanged. 555 more of the table's rows are removed or emptied wherever they appear, 56 of them sequences. Among them: Patient's Weight and Size (which PET SUV needs), Protocol Name, Contrast/Bolus Agent, ROI Name and Channel Label; Patient's Age under a `basic` config without the scaffold's `KEEP` (previously kept by omission); Encapsulated Document `(0042,0011)`, which the table gives `D` and is therefore written zero-length; and the date, time and name inside SR content items. Give any tag `action: KEEP` to retain it -- a user's own rule still wins over the base. A WFDB channel with no coded Channel Source is now named `ch<N>` even when its Channel Label was a known lead name, because the label is removed before export. The compliance report's method line reads `620 tag rules` where it read 36, which is also how to tell a 0.9.7 export's policy from a 0.9.8 one: the manifest records no policy. `create_config()` writes the same three research defaults, now in tag order (Study Date first).
  - **Audit volume grows with it.** Measured on a bare session over 2,000 copies of CT_small in 20 patients, each carrying a dozen identifiers the old profile missed, a Request Attributes Sequence, a Content Sequence and Overlay Comments (3.12, macOS, default worker strategy, two runs each): findings 396,060 -> 442,060 (198 -> 221 per instance, of which 179 are CT_small's private tags either way), audit-log rows 394,061 -> 440,061, `audit()` 2.7-3.0 s -> 3.1-4.0 s, `anonymize()` 5.3-5.9 s -> 6.9-8.4 s. Data carrying more of the table's attributes and fewer private tags grows proportionally more. The policy pickled into each patient's scan task grows from 1,603 to 29,921 bytes.
  - **Stores anonymized by 0.9.7 still read as anonymized.** An instance's PHI status belongs to its revision, not to the policy it was scanned under. A store remediated by 0.9.7 therefore reopens as `REMEDIATED`, its manifest says `anonymized: true`, and a plain `export()` writes the attributes 0.9.8 would now remove. **Run `audit()` and then `anonymize()` on such a store before exporting it again.** `export(check_burned_in=True)` re-audits first, and so **skips** those instances rather than writing them. Recording the policy with the status is #555.
  - **What this does not make conformant.** UIDs are not replaced, and the table's `U` rows have no rule (#544). Patient Identity Removed, De-identification Method and Longitudinal Temporal Information Modified are not written (#554). `D` codes are emptied rather than given a dummy value, so an attribute that is Type 1 in its IOD is written zero-length: measured, pydicom's `test-SR.dcm` exports zero-length Verifying Observer Name and Verification DateTime, pinned as such by `tests/test_sr_anonymization.py` so the dummy-value action (#557) flips it on purpose. Codes that depend on the IOD type are resolved by the rule above rather than by per-SOP-class type tables (#558). The retired Curve groups `(50xx)` are not removed, and removing Overlay Data `(60xx,3000)` -- written as sixteen concrete rules, one per even group, because the loader refuses mask keys -- leaves the rest of its Overlay Plane module (#556). Patient's Name, Patient ID and Study Date keep 0.9.7's rules and follow `anonymize()`'s own replacement (#537).
  - **Kept despite the table.** Study and Series Description are emptied, not removed, because the export directory names read them. Waveform Annotation Sequence (the Murmur annotation bridge reads it; its text and nested names are rows of their own and are cleaned) and Icon Image Sequence (dropped whenever pixels are redacted, #183) have no rule. Private attributes are the `remove_private_tags` sweep, not a rule. Isocenter's own redaction note in Derivation Description `(0008,2111)` is exempt by exact value -- without that, `export(check_burned_in=True)` would skip every redacted instance -- and any other Derivation Description is removed.
  - **Pins moved with it.** `DicomItem.clear_sequence_items()` is new and advances the revision only when it clears. The branch that uses it moves the five pinned `mark_modified()` lines in `remediation.py` to 291, 382, 432, 453 and 461 (`tests/test_remediation_invariants.py`). Profile membership is not frozen: it follows the named edition and can change in a minor release, listed under Breaking (`docs/api/stability.md` now says so).

### Fixed

- **Stale comments about the profile (#547).** `exporters/wfdb.py` said Acquisition DateTime and Study Time are removed by the basic profile; both have been emptied since #503 and this release, and the exporter reads an empty value as absent. `waveform.py` said a profile entry protects only sessions that loaded a configuration, which has been false since the floor (#495). `docs/api/stability.md` and `docs/configuration.md` gave Instance Creation Date as a date no shipped profile covers; the basic profile removes it now.

## [0.9.7] - 2026-09-12

### Security

- **Exported dates could be un-shifted, and exported Patient IDs reversed, from the exported files alone (GHSA-phg9-vcvc-j4r7).** Every release from 0.7.0 to 0.9.6 replaced Patient ID with `ANON_` plus the first 12 hex characters of an unsalted, unkeyed SHA-256 of the original, and derived each patient's date offset from the first 8 of those same characters. Measured on 0.9.6 with pydicom's `CT_small.dcm`: the export carries `PatientID = ANON_1c3ee9adf6f9` and `StudyDate = 20030525`; `(0x1c3ee9ad % 365) - 365 = -239`, and adding 239 days gives back `20040119`, the original, using nothing but the file and the documented default range. The same digest is a 48-bit unsalted hash of a low-entropy identifier: hashing every ID of the form `MRN0000000`–`MRN9999999` takes about 4.4 seconds on one CPU core, so the pseudonym is reversible for any ID drawn from a guessable space. Before 0.9.6 the offset was a fresh hash of the Patient ID, so the offset of every date shifted on the first pass could be read from the pseudonym in the same way; 0.9.6's #517 made that true of every pass. The documentation called the offset "secret"; it was not.
  - **Now.** Both are derived with HMAC-SHA256 under a 32-byte per-project secret that Isocenter generates on first use and stores inside the session store (a `project_secret` table), with distinct labels, so neither the pseudonym nor the offset reveals the other, and neither can be computed without the secret. The pseudonym is `ANON_` plus 24 hex characters: a 64-bit digest (collision probability 2.7e-6 at ten million patients, where 12 characters gave 0.16; a collision merges two patients under the store's `UNIQUE(patient_id)`) and a 32-bit check that lets Isocenter tell whether a secret it is given minted a store's pseudonyms. The secret is independent of `isocenter.key` and applies whether or not reversible anonymization is enabled. It is never written to an export, report, manifest, dataframe or log. There is no unkeyed fallback anywhere: a keyed derivation asked for without a secret raises `RuntimeError`.
  - **What this does not cover.** The fix is to the derivation: the offset can no longer be computed from the exported pseudonym or from anything else the derivation uses. It does not make every exported date unrecoverable. A date tag no rule shifts is exported as ingested -- Instance Creation Date `(0008,0012)` is covered by no shipped profile, and pydicom's `CT_small.dcm` carries the original date there on 0.9.6 and 0.9.7 alike -- UIDs that embed a date carry it (#544), and a whole-day shift keeps the weekday.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `anonymize()` on a new store writes a 29-character `ANON_` pseudonym and a different offset than 0.9.6 would have. Code that recomputed `sha256(PatientID)[:12]` to link a cohort across exports no longer matches, deliberately. Offsets are deterministic per patient **within a project**: one store, or stores sharing its secret through `session.store_backend.write_project_secret(path)` and `load_project_secret(path)`. Two stores that do not share it give the same patient different offsets, where 0.9.6 gave them the same one because anyone could compute it.
    - `audit()` and `anonymize()` -- including `anonymize(findings=...)`, which never enters `audit()` -- and `export(check_burned_in=True)`, which runs `audit()` before it writes, raise `RuntimeError: This store holds dates shifted under a project secret it no longer has (N patients) …` before any work, on a store with no secret row in which a keyed patient has any shifted date. The row is created before the first keyed shift can happen, so such a store lost its secret after shifting, and generating a new one would certainly give those patients a second offset inside the store. `write_project_secret` refuses the same store the same way. On a store with no secret yet, each of those calls generates one and commits it to the store, so a safe export is enough to give a store its secret (after which `load_project_secret` refuses it).
    - `load_project_secret(path)` raises `RuntimeError` on a store that already holds a project secret -- **any** secret, the same one included: anything the store pseudonymized or shifted was derived under the one it has. It raises `ValueError` for a file that is not exactly one `isocenter-project-secret-v1:<64 lowercase hex>` line, `ValueError` when the store holds keyed pseudonyms and the secret minted none of them, and `FileNotFoundError` for a missing file. So a project's secret is loaded into a fresh store, before its first `audit()` or `anonymize()`, either of which creates one. A store holding shifted dates but no keyed pseudonym to check a secret against (its patients kept their Patient IDs) accepts any well-formed secret file -- refusing would leave it no way back after losing its secret row -- records it as unverified (`project_secret.origin = 'loaded-unverified'`), and writes a `WARNING` row at the load and at every later `audit()`, so its reports grade `REVIEW_REQUIRED`: loaded with the wrong file, such a store gives a patient's later dates a second offset and has nothing left to detect it with. The record outlives the secret row: a store whose audit log holds that warning loads any later secret as unverified too, even one that verifies against its pseudonyms, because pseudonyms minted after an unverified load verify that load's secret and say nothing about the dates shifted before it. There is no call that clears the warning; a store that took a secret unverified grades `REVIEW_REQUIRED` for as long as its audit log exists.
    - `write_project_secret(path)` raises `FileExistsError` rather than overwrite, and creates the file with mode `0600`. A store with no secret yet gets one first.
    - `PhiInspector.scan_patient()` on an inspector built without `project_secret=` raises `RuntimeError` when it has to propose a keyed pseudonym, and `RemediationService._get_date_shift(patient_id, scheme)` takes the patient's scheme and raises `RuntimeError` for a keyed patient without a secret. Both classes are internal; `Session` passes the store's secret to both.
    - A fresh store that ingests another project's export and has no secret of its own generates one and writes a `WARNING` row naming the pseudonyms it cannot verify; a store that has a secret writes the same row on each `audit()` while such pseudonyms remain. Either grades the report `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. Starting a new project over another project's export therefore has one path -- let the new store generate its own secret and accept the warning -- unless the export's own secret is loaded into the fresh store first (see `docs/migration.md`).
  - **Stores de-identified by earlier releases.** Opening one classifies each patient once, into a new `patients.jitter_scheme` column, and never again: a class is written only into a NULL column and a save never overwrites one. A patient already de-identified -- its id has exactly the shape the old scheme minted (`ANON_` plus 12 lowercase hex), or any of its dates was shifted -- keeps the unkeyed scheme, both its old pseudonym and its old offset, because a keyed offset would put two offsets on one patient's dates, and their offset is already public through the pseudonym in every file exported for them. **Dates shifted for those patients by 0.9.7 are therefore still recoverable.** Every other patient, and every patient added later, is keyed. Each open writes one `WARNING` audit row naming how many patients keep the old scheme, and how many carry an old pseudonym from a re-ingested pre-0.9.7 export (an id already `ANON_` is never replaced, so it is exported unchanged), so every compliance report over such a store grades `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; `audit()` repeats the second count, so a session that ingests such an export and exports it again is told in its own report. Raw files ingested for a patient the store de-identified before 0.9.7 are a new, keyed subject with a different offset, and `audit()` writes a `WARNING` row saying so. The remedy is to re-ingest the **source** files into a new store. Files already exported by an earlier release stay recoverable, and no release can change that: treat their dates and Patient IDs as identifiable.
  - **Supersedes part of 0.9.6's #517 entry.** "No offset changes for a patient whose id has not been replaced" and "there is no migration" described the unkeyed arithmetic that is the defect. The #517 guarantee itself (a date first shifted in a later pass, or in a re-ingested export, lands on its patient's offset) holds for keyed patients, and for a re-ingested export only when the store holds the same project secret. `privacy.jitter_digest`, which that entry named, is gone, not aliased; the unkeyed derivations survive only as private functions reachable for patients classed unkeyed.
  - **The working store is sensitive.** It already recorded each original Patient ID beside its pseudonym, and each offset, in its audit log. It now also holds the project secret, which recovers the dates of every store sharing that secret. Never ship the `.db` with an export.
  - **`isocenter.log` no longer names patients or offsets.** Every earlier release logged `Remediated <original Patient ID>: patient_id -> <pseudonym>` and `Date Shifted <UID>: study_date (<N> days)` at `INFO`, and `lock_identities` logged the Patient ID at `DEBUG`, `INFO` and `ERROR`: the log file held the same ID-to-pseudonym map and every offset the store's audit log does, without being guarded as the store is. Those lines now name the UID, the field and counts (`Remediated patient_id on a patient; 1 instance copy`, `Date Shifted study_date on <StudyInstanceUID>`). The audit rows are unchanged. A test drives ingest, identity locking, audit, anonymize, export and identity recovery under threads and processes and searches the log at `DEBUG` and the console for the original Patient ID, the original date in DA, ISO and `date` spellings, and the offset signed, unsigned or as a number of days, weeks or months. `recover_patient_identity()` still prints the Patient ID it is given when no patient has it, as it always has (filed separately). Log files written by earlier releases carry the map and the offsets: treat them as the store.

### Breaking

- **BREAKING: new `ANON_` pseudonym shape and keyed date offsets (GHSA-phg9-vcvc-j4r7).** See Security above for every call whose result or exception changed.
- **BREAKING: `session.scan_worker` accepts exactly `(patient, config_source, remove_private, project_secret)`.** The three- and two-element forms, and the `(db_path, patient_id, config_source, remove_private)` form, which no code path used, now raise `ValueError` on unpacking or `TypeError` for a non-`Patient` first element. The secret travels by value in the tuple: a worker cannot read it from a `:memory:` store, and a second place to find a secret is a second answer to which one keys a patient.

### Changed

- **The user documentation now states what 0.9.0 through 0.9.6 actually ship (#545, #546).** A changelog-driven audit found most drift was absence rather than falsity. The README and eleven docs pages were corrected: private binary retention by size since #151, the floor policy, how the report is graded and what its sections are, the spawn main guard, default compression's colour relabelling, `verify_readback`, the export layout, POSIX-only support, and worker defaults. The behaviour defects the audit found are filed as #536-#544, #547 and #548.

### Corrections to earlier entries

- **0.9.6, #502: "`WARNING` is one of the five action types #411 froze" is wrong.** The frozen audit `action_type` vocabulary is thirteen words (`docs/api/stability.md`, `tests/test_frozen_surface.py`). #411 added four `REMEDIATION_*` words and the `AUDIT_DROP` report category to the freeze; `WARNING` was frozen before it. The rule the entry meant (reuse `WARNING`, invent no new action type) stands.
- **0.9.6, #495: "`action: KEEP` on a tag to opt that one out" is false for three tags.** Patient's Name, Patient ID and Study Date are replaced by `anonymize()` under every profile, whatever their rule says. `KEEP`, `REMOVE`, `EMPTY` and `REPLACE` on those three are tracked in #537.

## [0.9.6] - 2026-09-12

### Breaking

- **BREAKING: `Instance.date_shifted` is gone (#510).** `instance.date_shifted` on an `Instance` reached from `session.store` now raises `AttributeError: 'Instance' object has no attribute 'date_shifted'`. It was a field on the frozen entity shape (`docs/api/stability.md`, `Instance`'s dataclass order) and is deleted rather than deprecated, per the pre-1.0 convention that duplicate and dead surface is removed, not aliased.
  - **Why it was wrong to keep.** It was never persisted -- the `instances` table has no column for it, unlike `studies.date_shifted` (#182) -- so a loaded instance reported `False` however many of its dates had been shifted, and the value a caller read depended on whether the session had been reopened. It was also an entity-level boolean speaking for an unbounded set of values: it went `True` when any one date on the instance shifted and said nothing about which, which is the defect #510 and #513 are. After those fixes nothing in the pipeline read it at all.
  - **What answers the question now.** "Was *this* value shifted?" is answered per value, by the record the `SHIFT_DATE` arm writes (`DicomItem._shifted_dates`; private, tier 3, so not a name to program against). "Did a de-identifying shift run on this study?" is `Study.date_shifted`, which is **unchanged** -- still a public field, still persisted, still what the WFDB header's `# de-identified start date:` comment is derived from (`exporters/wfdb.py`), and now also the only persisted witness the pre-0.9.6 rule in #510 can read. There is no replacement for the instance-level flag because there was no honest question it answered: a caller that needs to know whether an instance is de-identified should read `phi_status` or the audit trail, both of which are per-entity facts the store keeps.
  - **Pins updated with it, on purpose.** `tests/test_frozen_surface.py`'s `FROZEN_INSTANCE_FIELDS` loses the name, and the field is now pinned as *absent* in both directions -- re-adding it is red, because the superset check that guards that list would have been green for a field that came back. `docs/api/stability.md` says the field is gone rather than merely omitting it, and that sentence is pinned too. The `==` pins on `Patient`, `Study` and `Series` are untouched. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-frozen-surface-and-strategy-bunch-3.md` carries a `Superseded in part` note for the two clauses that froze the field.

- **BREAKING: an export that would write more than one Photometric Interpretation onto a file with pixel data is refused instead of delivered (#502).** (0028,0004) is VM 1, and a graph carrying `['YBR_ICT', 'RGB']` was written as a two-value CS element -- measured on `a50632d`, on both gate interpreters, with `verify_readback=True` passing it and the run grading `PASS`. Such a file **with pixel data** cannot be read back by this library at all: `session.ingest()` refuses it with `Decompression Failed: TypeError: unhashable type: 'MultiValue'` (3.12.14; 3.14.7t words the same `TypeError` differently) -- the decompression step hashes the label before anything examines it, which is why this one case is refused where an inadmissible single label is written with a warning. A previously-working `DicomExporter.write_tree()` on such a graph now raises `RuntimeError("Export incomplete. 1 failed. First error: PhotometricInterpretation (0028,0004) is a single value; this instance declares 2 ('YBR_ICT', 'RGB'). ...")`, and `session.export()` audits one `ERROR` row, counts the instance in `ExportSummary.failures`, grades the run `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, and delivers every other instance -- raising `ExportError` only if nothing reached disk. The new exception is `io_handlers._PhotometricRefusal`, a `RuntimeError` subclass, so every existing handler sees what it saw before. **The refusal is judged on the dataset the file will carry, not on the declaration:** at one sample the geometry resolver has already answered `MONOCHROME2`, so a *monochrome* instance whose declaration is multi-valued still exports, single-valued and re-ingestible, with `ok=True` and no warning -- refusing it would have denied the caller an output this library can read back, which is the one thing the exception is not for.
  - **Scope, measured, and narrower than "every export": the two arms that write a pixel element.** The check lives in `_write_pixel_geometry`, which both the integer and the float pixel arms call, so neither can bypass it. An instance with **no pixel element at all** never reaches that function, and `_merge` has already put the declared `0028,0004` onto the dataset -- so an SR-shaped instance declaring `['YBR_ICT', 'RGB']` is still exported with `ok=True`, and the file still reads back `MultiValue(['YBR_ICT', 'RGB'])`. The same arm still writes a single inadmissible label such as `YBR_ICT` in silence, with `ExportOutcome.warnings` empty. `export(verify_readback=True)` catches both, because #507's check reads the delivered file and does not care which arm wrote it. That third arm is **filed for v0.9.7 and deliberately not closed here**: routing it through this check is new behaviour needing its own tests, and reaching it takes a malformed source or a hand-built graph -- a pixel descriptor on an instance with no pixels.
  - **Why this one label is refused when an inadmissible one is written with a warning.** The ruling on the write path is warn and attempt the best output: there are formats this library can read and cannot write, and a de-identified copy plus a row saying what could not be honoured beats no copy. Refusal is the exception, for when no output would be honest -- and here there is none: no single value can be chosen without inventing one, and a file carrying both is one this library could not read back. That is the standard `_J2K_ENCODABLE_FRAMES` already refuses a frame on.

- **BREAKING: `export(verify_readback=True)` refuses a file whose Photometric Interpretation the transfer syntax it was written under does not admit (#507).** `verify_readback=True` presents the stronger claim -- "a file exists that decodes to what we meant" -- and did not check the one element that names what the samples are. Measured on `a50632d`, on both gate interpreters, over an 8x8x3 `uint8` array under Implicit VR Little Endian: an instance declaring `YBR_ICT`, `YBR_RCT`, `YBR_PARTIAL_422` or `YBR_PARTIAL_420` passed verification with `ok=True`, the audit log was empty and the report read `PASS`. A file carrying `['YBR_ICT', 'RGB']` passed too. The descriptor pass compares `_READBACK_DESCRIPTORS` -- `Rows`, `Columns`, `SamplesPerPixel`, `NumberOfFrames`, `BitsAllocated` -- and `PhotometricInterpretation` was never in that tuple at all. A previously-passing `session.export(folder, verify_readback=True)` on such an instance now fails that instance. The export worker's `ExportOutcome` carries `ok=False` and `RuntimeError("Readback verification failed: PhotometricInterpretation reads back as 'YBR_ICT', which the transfer syntax the file was written under does not admit (1.2.840.10008.1.2): these two labels name the irreversible and reversible multiple-component transforms of a JPEG 2000 codestream, and an uncompressed file has no codestream to carry one. Export with use_compression=True, ...")`; `session.export()` returns an `ExportSummary` with the instance in `.failures`, writes one `ERROR` audit row, grades the run `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, **delivers no file for it** -- the check fires against the temporary file, before the rename that publishes it (#199) -- and raises `ExportError` only if nothing at all reached disk. `DicomExporter.write_tree()` is unaffected: it takes no `verify_readback` parameter and never has, so the serializer path writes such a file as it did before, with #502's `WARNING` and nothing else. A multi-valued label in the file fails with `... is VM 1; the written file reads back as 2 values ('YBR_ICT', 'RGB')`. Two files reach that clause: a hand-built one, and one this library wrote from an instance with **no pixel element**, which #502's writer-side check never sees (see its entry above). The reason names the arity rather than re-ingestibility, because measured, "this library cannot re-ingest it" is true only of a file with pixel data -- `ingest()` refuses the `MultiValue` while decompressing -- and false of a pixel-less one, which comes back as `IngestSummary(ingested=1, failures=[])` with the graph carrying both values. For the same reason the remedy offered for a single inadmissible label checks for a pixel element first: `Export with use_compression=True` is no help to an instance with nothing to compress, and such a file is told so instead.
  - **This is the first descriptor on which `verify_readback=True` refuses something the export worker wrote on purpose, and that is the contract, not an implementation detail.** Everything the readback refused before was a file the worker meant to be correct. Since #502 the *default* write path deliberately writes an inadmissible label as declared, with a `WARNING` audit row and a `REVIEW_REQUIRED` grade, because there are formats this library can read and cannot write and a de-identified copy the caller can fix beats no copy. `verify_readback=True` is the caller who asked for the stronger claim, and the two answers to the same file now differ on purpose: best effort by default, conformance on request. What a caller gets that they did not have before is a **demand for conformant output** -- a run that grades `PASS` with `verify_readback=True` now also asserts that every delivered label is one its syntax admits. What they lose is the file for an instance whose header was impossible; the fix is the remedy sentence in the reason, or the default path, which still delivers it.
  - **No new flag, deliberately.** A third setting (`verify_readback="lenient"`, or a `refuse_inadmissible_labels=` parameter) was considered and rejected: #26 is the API-freeze issue for 1.0 and this is not the moment to widen the public surface, and two contracts are the two that were asked for. `tests/test_frozen_surface.py` pins the `export()` signature unchanged.
  - **The limit, documented rather than fixed, and #507 closes with it.** The check is *structural*: it asks whether a conformant reader could take this label under this syntax, driven by `io_handlers._ADMISSIBLE_PHOTOMETRICS` -- the three uncompressed syntaxes share a row, JPEG 2000 Lossless adds `YBR_ICT`, `YBR_RCT` and the two `YBR_PARTIAL_*`. It does not ask whether the samples are really in the colour space the label names, because that has no answer from the bytes -- three samples are equally `RGB` and `YBR_FULL` -- and #372/#448/#482 is the standing ruling that this library neither makes nor checks a claim the bytes cannot prove. So `RGB` over YBR samples still passes, and a file under a syntax with no row passes rather than being judged against a table nobody measured (this library decodes eight transfer syntaxes it cannot write -- #526). `PhotometricInterpretation` was **not** added to `_READBACK_DESCRIPTORS`: every keyword there is compared against the dataset the worker serialized, and the worker writes that label onto that dataset itself, so both sides would come from one assignment and agree however the writer was broken -- a comparison that cannot fail, which reads in a diff like a check. The syntax the label has to be held against is not on that dataset at all; it is in `file_meta`.
  - **The one reader that sees a compressed file's final label.** `_write_pixel_geometry` runs before `_compress_j2k`, so #502's write-path warning judges the label the writer put on the dataset, and under JPEG 2000 the encoder then relabels an `RGB` source `YBR_RCT` (#516 case 1). The readback is downstream of that relabel, and all three of #516's cases pass it: `RGB` -> `YBR_RCT`, a source already `YBR_RCT`/`YBR_ICT` keeping its label (#490's ruling), and every other 3-sample source keeping its label under `mct=False`. A table narrowed to `YBR_RCT` alone would have refused this library's own output.

- **BREAKING: a session that has loaded no configuration now de-identifies against a floor policy (#495).** Measured on `168fdd6` with pydicom's `CT_small.dcm`: `Session` -> `ingest` -> `audit()` -> `anonymize()` -> `export()` wrote a file carrying Study ID `1CT1`, Series/Acquisition/Content Date `19970430`, Station Name `CT01_OC0`, Institution Name `JFK IMAGING CENTER`, Study Time `072730`, Study Description and three more times, with the report graded `PASS` and its method line saying `Session defaults: 6 tag rules` -- six rules the scan never applied, because `audit()` read `configuration.phi_tags` (`{}`) and the report read the shipped `phi_tags.json`. The bare `phi_tags` is now `profiles.FLOOR_POLICY`: the PS3.15 basic profile plus the three research defaults `create_config()` has always written (Study Date jittered, Sex and Age kept), 36 rules. The scaffold is generated from the same table (the floor diffed against the basic profile), so it cannot drift from what a bare session applies.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `anonymize()` on a bare session removes or empties 33 more tags than before. **`load_config()` of a file with `phi_tags` and no `privacy_profile` line now applies the floor beneath those tags**: measured before, a one-tag file loaded one rule and Study ID `1CT1` and Institution Name reached the export; it now loads 37. Write `privacy_profile: none` to load only your own tags, or `action: KEEP` on a tag to opt that one out; the loader logs `applying the floor policy` when it does this. `export(check_burned_in=True)` on a session that has not run `anonymize()` now skips every instance carrying a floor tag with a value, where it skipped only those whose patient name, ID or study date was still real: a patient named `ANONYMIZED` whose instance carries a real Study Time was written before and is skipped now (`tests/test_safe_export.py` pins it). A bare session's WFDB header loses its base time -- the floor empties Study Time and removes Acquisition DateTime -- and carries the shifted date in its `# de-identified start date:` comment instead. `generate_report` counts the policy in force with no fallback: a bare session reads `36 tag rules`, and `privacy_profile: none` with no tags reads `0 tag rules`, where the fallback would have named rules the scan never ran.
  - **Also changed.** `resources/phi_tags.json` is deleted -- six name-only tags, all already in the basic profile, read only by the default loader, the scaffold's tag names and the report's count -- and `ConfigLoader.load_phi_config()` with no path returns a copy of the floor, which is what `PhiInspector()` with no policy now scans against. `publish.yml`'s wheel gate reads `redaction_rules.json` through `require_package_resource`, since a gate on the floor would pass on a wheel shipping nothing. `set_phi_tag` stores lowercase keys: it uppercased, so `0008,103E` sat beside the floor's `0008,103e` as a second rule for one tag, and which won was dict order; the loader lowercases a file's keys before the merge for the same reason. `save()` writes `privacy_profile: none` rather than the unknown name `custom`, which #456 below would refuse at reload. The scaffold's tag names now come from the profile (`Patient's Sex`, `Patient's Age`). Where the first instance no longer carries its own Patient's Name or Patient ID, `lock_identities` now stashes the patient's, and it raises `RuntimeError` when any value it is about to stash -- a copy, or that patient value -- reads `ANONYMIZED` or starts `ANON_`. #492's refusal and the stash read only the instance copies, which the floor removes. Measured on `CT_small.dcm`: lock -> anonymize -> lock again raised nothing, and lock -> an instance-only `anonymize()` -> lock again (the patient still holding the originals, so rightly not refused) stashed the copies alone. Both wrote a token holding only `{'0010,0040': 'O'}` over the good one, so recovery lost the name and ID.

- **BREAKING: `load_config()` raises instead of printing `Load failed` and leaving an empty policy (#456).** Every validation failure is `ValueError` -- a file that is not `.yaml`/`.yml`, YAML syntax (`ValueError: Invalid YAML format in <path>: ...`, where `yaml.parser.ParserError` escaped the loader), a root that is not a mapping (an empty file, a scalar, a list: `TypeError`/`AttributeError` before), an unknown `privacy_profile` or a custom-profile path that does not exist, an `action` outside `KEEP`/`REMOVE`/`EMPTY`/`REPLACE`/`SHIFT`/`JITTER`, a `phi_tags` that is not a mapping or a tag value that is neither a name nor a rule, a `phi_tags` key that is not `gggg,eeee` hex (`'8,80'`, `PatientName`: the scan reads no tag by such a key, so the rule loaded and never ran), an external profile file with no `phi_tags:` mapping (its root was taken as the tags, so a profile written like a config loaded `privacy_profile` as a tag), a `date_jitter` that is neither an int nor `{min_days: int, max_days: int}`, a `machines` that is not a list of mappings, a rule `_validate_rule` rejects (a zone of strings now included, which escaped as `TypeError`) -- and a missing file is `FileNotFoundError`. The configuration is exactly what it was before the call: nothing is assigned until the loader has returned.
  - **Before.** Measured on `168fdd6` over 21 inputs. `load_config` caught every exception, printed `Load failed: ...` and a traceback beside an ERROR log carrying the same text, set `rules = []`, `phi_tags = {}` and `privacy_profile = None`, and returned `None`. So a file that failed validation wiped the policy the session already had, and a script that ignored stdout went on to audit against nothing. Four shapes were not refused at all: `action: OBLITERATE` loaded and was scanned as `REPLACE`; a list-shaped `phi_tags` loaded and broke the scan's `.items()` later; `'0010,0010': 7` loaded as a display name; an unknown profile (`comprehensive`, which the README offered) was warned about and dropped, loading the file's tags with no base. `date_jitter: soon` and `{days: 3}` were accepted by the loader and failed in `load_config`'s own print *after* the assignments, leaving `date_jitter='soon'` in the session beside the emptied fields, with `config_path` pointing at the failed file.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** Any of those files, which returned normally, now raises -- and a session that had a policy keeps it. A custom profile file that fails to load raises too, where it was logged and skipped. `audit(config_path=)` raises the same way: its fallback to a plain tag-file reader is gone, so a `.json` file (accepted there, refused by `load_config`) raises `ValueError`, and so does a file whose rule the loader rejects (audited happily before). A root-level tag file with no `phi_tags` key, which that fallback accepted, now loads as a config with no tags; its tag was never matched by the scan anyway. **Exception types**: `ValueError` and `FileNotFoundError`, deliberately no new `ConfigError` -- `__all__` is frozen at five names, and a `ConfigError(ValueError)` can be added in 1.x without breaking a caller who catches `ValueError`.
  - This closes two references in this changelog: the "separate, pre-existing silence, filed as its own issue" in the #424 entry below (docs/ocr.md's published YAML printed `Load failed` and left the session with no rules), and the mutation probe's `session.py` survivor "a print beside an ERROR log that carries the same text". Pinned by `tests/test_load_config_raises.py`, which sets a sentinel in each of the six fields before every one of the 21 inputs and asserts all six survive.

- **BREAKING: an *unsigned* JPEG 2000 codestream under PixelRepresentation 1 is read by the header at every door, where the handler returned the codec's unsigned array, and a *signed* codestream under PixelRepresentation 0 now raises at the imagecodecs handler -- at every door for 16-bit colour, and at that one door only for monochrome and 8-bit colour (#460).** `imagecodecs.jpeg2k_decode` returns the codestream's own signedness, whatever the header declares, so one file carried two answers in both directions. **The two halves of the fix do not have the same reach, and the scope below is measured rather than inferred:** the reinterpretation reaches every door, the refusal reaches every door only where pydicom's Pillow plugin cannot decode the file.

  - **Before.** Measured on 336eade (3.12.14, pydicom 3.0.2, imagecodecs 2026.8.16). *Unsigned under 1:* pydicom's own `J2K_pixelrep_mismatch.dcm` -- a CT from pydicom issue 1149, unsigned precision-13 codestream, BitsStored 13, HighBit 12 -- read `int16 [-2000, 1896]` at `ingest()` and at `Instance.get_pixel_data()`, which reach pydicom's Pillow plugin for 16-bit monochrome J2K, and `uint16 [0, 8191]` from `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()`: the codestream's patterns, 6192 where the file means -2000. Where the handler was the only decoder -- 16-bit colour, which Pillow refuses -- `ingest()` refused the file instead (`it decoded to uint16, where BitsAllocated 16 and PixelRepresentation 1 declare int16`) while both read doors returned the patterns with no error. *Signed under 0:* the handler and the Instance door returned `int16` under a header declaring unsigned samples, with no error, and `ingest()` refused it (`it decoded to int16, where … declare uint16`).
  - **Now, the owner's ruling.** The two directions are not symmetrical and are not treated alike. An unsigned codestream under PixelRepresentation 1 is **reinterpreted by the header**, through the same `_sign_extend` the JPEG rules use, at the *codestream's* precision. A signed codestream under PixelRepresentation 0 is **refused**. Both decisions are made in `_decode_frame`, which all three doors reach -- but reaching that code is not the same as reaching that answer, because `ingest()` and `Instance.get_pixel_data()` try pydicom first (#416) and only fall back to this handler when pydicom fails. So the number of answers per file depends on whether Pillow can decode it, and **only the reinterpretation is one answer everywhere** (its files read alike whichever decoder answers). See *Which doors the refusal reaches* below. `J2K_pixelrep_mismatch.dcm` now reads `int16 [-2000, 1896]` at all four of ingest, the Instance door, the handler and pydicom -- measured on 3.12.14 and on 3.14.7t, which read it identically -- and the 16-bit colour shape ingests with its values instead of being refused.
  - **Why reinterpret one and refuse the other.** For the unsigned-under-1 direction there is a pydicom answer to match and a real file to match it on, and pydicom's rule is exactly this one (`pixels.decoders.base._apply_sign_correction`, keyed on `j2k_precision` and `j2k_is_signed` from the SIZ segment). For signed-under-0 there is no single pydicom answer to agree with: pydicom's correction is gated on a nonzero bit shift, so at a precision equal to the container's it does nothing and the value returned is whatever the plugin reinterpreted -- for a codestream holding `[-32768, -800, -1]`, pydicom 3.0.2 with Pillow returns `uint16 [0, 31968, 32767]` and with pylibjpeg-openjpeg `uint16 [32768, 64736, 65535]` (measured). Two plugins, two arrays, neither of them the file's samples. For the 16-bit colour shape, which Pillow cannot decode, ingest already refused the file, so refusing at the handler is what makes the three doors say one thing rather than adding a fourth answer.
  - **The precision is the codestream's, not BitsStored.** Where they differ the two give different arrays, and only the codestream's matches pydicom: a precision-12 unsigned codestream under BitsStored 16 and PixelRepresentation 1 reads `-800` for the pattern 3296 (shift 4), where reading by BitsStored shifts by nothing and returns 3296. `_j2k_sample_layout` reads it from `Ssiz^0` in the SIZ marker segment (ISO/IEC 15444-1 A.5.1), walking SOC → SIZ rather than searching for `FF 51`, and unwrapping a JP2 box first -- this project itself wrote that box under 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.90 until #404, so every JPEG 2000 file Isocenter exported before that release is JP2-wrapped and must reach the same rule.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()` and `Instance.get_pixel_data()` on an unsigned J2K codestream under PixelRepresentation 1 return the signed dtype the header declares, holding different values: `int16 -2000` where they returned `uint16 6192`. Code that re-signed the pattern itself now double-corrects. A file `ingest()` refused for that dtype mismatch now ingests. And a read of a *signed* codestream under PixelRepresentation 0, which returned `int16` values, now raises `RuntimeError: … the JPEG 2000 codestream is signed at precision 16, where PixelRepresentation 0 declares unsigned samples: `jpeg2k_decode` returns the codestream's own signedness, and there is no unsigned reading of these samples this handler can stand behind -- pydicom returns a different array for such a file with each of its two JPEG 2000 plugins`. From `Instance.get_pixel_data()` those words arrive on the `imagecodecs fallback:` line of `Lazy load failed for <path>: …` (measured). Not `Failed to decompress pixel data for <file> …`: that carrier is chosen by a `"missing dependencies" in str(e) or "decompress" in str(e)` test on pydicom's own error, and Pillow's refusal here -- `Pillow cannot decode 16-bit multi-sample data correctly` -- contains neither word. The JPEG syntaxes do land on `Failed to decompress`; this J2K path is the exception. `ingest()`'s row carries the same words after `imagecodecs could not decode it either:`. **Two further raises come with the reinterpretation, because it runs through `_sign_extend` and inherits that function's guards, and both are reachable by a call that used to return an array.** An unsigned codestream under PixelRepresentation 1 whose HighBit is not BitsStored - 1 now raises the #446 refusal (`HighBit 15 with BitsStored 12: a JPEG decode returns right-aligned 12-bit samples, …`), where the handler returned the codec's `uint16` and pydicom -- which ignores HighBit entirely for JPEG 2000 -- returns `int16` (measured: `int16 [0, 1500]` for a pattern the handler now refuses), so this is a divergence from pydicom that #446's ruling produces rather than a new decision here. And a codestream whose precision is 8 or less under BitsStored greater than 8 raises `cannot sign-extend a uint8 decode from BitsStored 12: the codec returns unsigned samples at most 8 bits wide`, where the handler returned the `uint8` the codec gave it. Whether HighBit should gate a JPEG 2000 read at all is not decided here -- #446 answered it for the JPEG syntaxes and this route arrives at the same guard.
  - **Which doors the refusal reaches, measured.** All three doors run `_decode_frame`, but `ingest()` and `Instance.get_pixel_data()` reach it only when pydicom has already failed (#416 made the read doors pydicom-first), and pydicom's Pillow plugin decodes more JPEG 2000 than it is given credit for. Measured on this branch, for a signed codestream under PixelRepresentation 0:
    - **16-bit colour** -- Pillow refuses it (`Pillow cannot decode 16-bit multi-sample data correctly`), so all three doors fall through to the handler and all three now refuse. One answer per file, which is what this half of the fix was for.
    - **Monochrome at any depth, and 8-bit colour** -- Pillow decodes it, so `ingest()` still admits the file with no error and no `DATA_LOSS` row, and `Instance.get_pixel_data()` still returns Pillow's reading: the codestream's samples with the sign bit flipped, `source + 2**(bits-1)` exactly (a precision-16 monochrome codestream holding `[-32768, 32767]` reads `uint16 [0, 65535]`). Only `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()` refuses. **These files carry two answers, and the refusal creates that disagreement at one door rather than resolving it.**
    So the refusal half of option C is structurally handler-only for everything Pillow can read. That is a deliberate limit and not an oversight: making it reach ingest means gating pydicom's J2K decode on the SIZ header before pydicom is asked, which is a separate design call the owner is deciding. `test_which_doors_refuse_a_signed_codestream_under_pixel_representation_0` pins today's answer at all three doors, so that change will be visible rather than silent.
  - **Unchanged.** A codestream whose signedness agrees with its header, in either state, is returned exactly as the codec decoded it -- the rule fires only on the disagreement. Nothing about JPEG Lossless, JPEG-LS or baseline JPEG moves; `_sign_extend` is reached from the J2K arm in one case only, and never for a signed codestream. A bitstream whose SIZ does not parse, which no successful decode can be, leaves the array untouched rather than guessing. Pinned at all three doors, on 3.12 and 3.14t, by `tests/test_j2k_signedness_against_pixel_representation.py` (16 cases including the real file and the JP2 wrapper); `tests/test_signed_lossless_jpeg_decode.py`'s S4, which pinned the old refusal, now pins the reinterpretation and is the boundary between the two rules.

- **BREAKING: `Instance.get_pixel_data()` returns a JPEG Lossless or JPEG-LS stream of precision 8 or less under BitsAllocated 16 in that 16-bit container, `uint16` or `int16`, where it returned `uint8` or `int8`, and `ingest()` now accepts these files (#454).** A frozen method's return dtype changes for these files. The values do not.

  - **Before.** Measured on 336eade (3.12.14, pydicom 3.0.2, imagecodecs 2026.8.16). The files were under 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.57, .70, .80 or .81 with BitsAllocated 16 and BitsStored 8. In the environment this package installs, pydicom has no plugin for those syntaxes, so both read doors reach the imagecodecs fallback. There, `Instance.get_pixel_data()` and `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()` returned `uint8 [0, 1, 2, 3, …]`, or `int8 [-128, -1, 0, 127, …]` when signed: the right values in the wrong container. `ingest()` refused the same file: `imagecodecs could not decode it either: it decoded to uint8, where BitsAllocated 16 and PixelRepresentation 0 declare uint16`. A precision-8 JPEG-LS stream under a signed BitsStored 12 was refused at all three doors: `cannot sign-extend a uint8 decode from BitsStored 12`.
  - **Now.** The handler widens the codec's `uint8` to `uint16` whenever BitsAllocated is 16. It does this in `_decode_frame`, which all three doors reach, and before the sign extension, so a signed sample is extended inside `int16`. All three doors return `uint16` or `int16` holding the same values, and `ingest()` accepts the file. The BitsStored-12 stream reads `int16`, sign-extended from its own precision 8 (#478): the patterns 128..255 read −128..−1.
  - **Against pydicom.** For JPEG-LS this is pydicom's answer. pydicom 3.0.2 with pyjpegls 1.5.1 returns `uint16`/`int16` for every one of these streams, the BitsStored-12 one included, where it reads −128..127 (measured). For JPEG Lossless there is no pydicom answer to match. pydicom with pylibjpeg-libjpeg raises on every precision-8 stream under BitsAllocated 16 (`could not broadcast input array from shape (128,) into shape (256,)`), so there the three doors agree with each other rather than with pydicom. dcmtk 3.7.0's `dcmdjpls` refuses the JPEG-LS files outright: `Image data mismatch between DICOM header and JPEG-LS bitstream`.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `get_pixel_data()` on such a file returns `uint16` or `int16` where it returned `uint8` or `int8`, so the array is twice the size and holds the same values. Code that compared the dtype with `uint8`, or read `arr.nbytes`, sees the change. Code that widened the array itself gets the same values it did. A file `ingest()` refused now ingests.
  - **Unchanged.** A header whose container cannot hold BitsStored at all, BitsStored 12 under BitsAllocated 8, is refused as before and in the same words. Only a `uint8` decode under BitsAllocated 16 is widened. A decode wider than its container is left for the dtype guard to refuse. JPEG 2000 and baseline JPEG are not touched. Pinned by S6 (now a JPEG Lossless stream under BitsAllocated 8, so it still kills the probe's `or`→`and` mutant on its guard), S7, S7a and S7b in `tests/test_signed_lossless_jpeg_decode.py`, at all three doors, on 3.12 and 3.14t.

- **BREAKING: `Instance.get_pixel_data()` returns signed JPEG Lossless and JPEG-LS pixels as the signed values they are, where it returned their unsigned bit patterns, and a signed frame whose HighBit is not BitsStored − 1 now raises (#446).** A frozen method's return dtype changes for these files, from unsigned to the signed dtype the header declares.

  - **Before.** Measured on 6aabc7d, for a signed (PixelRepresentation 1) file under 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.57, .70, .80 or .81, which pydicom cannot decode in the environment this package installs. The imagecodecs fallback returned `uint16 [3296, 4095, 0, 2000]` for stored values `[-800, -1, 0, 2000]` at BitsStored 12, and `uint16 [64736, 65535, 0, 2000]` at BitsStored 16, with no error: `imagecodecs.ljpeg_decode` and `jpegls_decode` return the masked unsigned pattern of every sample at every BitsStored, and nothing sign-extended it. `ingest()` refused the same files since #416 (`decoded to uint16, where BitsAllocated 16 and PixelRepresentation 1 declare int16`), so the two doors disagreed, and the one that answered answered wrongly.
  - **Now.** Both doors return `int16`, or `int8` where BitsAllocated is also 8, holding the values the file stores, and `ingest()` accepts these files. The handler sign-extends in `_decode_frame`, which both doors reach, from BitsStored or, for a JPEG-LS stream, from the stream's own precision (#478, below), so there is one rule rather than a guard at one door and a fix at the other. It is the rule pydicom applies with its own plugins, measured bit-exact against pydicom with pylibjpeg-libjpeg and pyjpegls at 8, 12 and 16 bits, and pinned here at 8, 12 and 16 bits under all four syntaxes, with two LJPEG encoders and a precision-12 JPEG-LS stream from CharLS, at `ingest()`, `Instance.get_pixel_data()` and the handler, on 3.12 and 3.14t (`tests/test_signed_lossless_jpeg_decode.py`).
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `get_pixel_data()` on such a file returns a different dtype and different values; code that re-signed the pattern itself (`arr.astype(np.int16)` after masking, or a manual two's-complement fix) now double-corrects. And a signed file under those syntaxes whose HighBit is not BitsStored − 1, for which `get_pixel_data()` returned the unsigned pattern, now raises `RuntimeError: Failed to decompress pixel data for <file> (Transfer Syntax: <uid>). … imagecodecs fallback: imagecodecs failed to decode <uid>: HighBit 15 with BitsStored 12: a JPEG decode returns right-aligned 12-bit samples, so a signed sample is sign-extended from BitsStored only when HighBit is BitsStored - 1`, and `ingest()` refuses it with the same words. A JPEG decoder returns right-aligned samples, so there is no reading of such a header that the decoder's output supports; ignoring HighBit, as pydicom does, and shifting from it would each return a value the file does not hold. This follows the recommended answer to an owner question and awaits confirmation. An unsigned file with the same header is returned untouched, as pydicom returns it.
  - **A JPEG-LS stream is read by its own precision where that differs from BitsStored, as pydicom with pyjpegls reads it (#478).** That is the owner's ruling, and it reverses the BitsStored reading this entry first shipped with. `imagecodecs.jpegls_encode` cannot write precision 12, so it writes a 12-bit pattern under BitsStored 12 as a precision-16 stream, and that stream now reads 3296 for −800's pattern, not −800. The other direction reads the same way: a precision-12 stream under BitsStored 16 reads −800, where the BitsStored reading returned 3296. So does a precision-16 stream holding an 8-bit pattern under BitsStored 8, which reads 128 where it read −128. All three rows match pydicom with pyjpegls (3.12.14, pydicom 3.0.2, pyjpegls 1.5.1). A precision-12 stream under BitsStored 12, as a conformant encoder writes it, still reads −800. Each frame is read by its own header's precision, which is pydicom's per-frame answer (`pixel_array(path, index=i)`). pydicom's whole-array read applies the *last* frame's precision to every frame, so `[P12, P16]` reads 3296 in both frames there; here it reads −800 and then 3296. The precision is found by walking the segments to the SOF55 header, not by searching for `FF F7`, which a COM or APPn payload may hold. JPEG Lossless (.57, .70) keeps BitsStored: pydicom reads it that way too (`_correct_unused_bits`), and a precision-16 SOF3 stream under BitsStored 12 still reads −800. **One divergence from pydicom remains, stated.** It was measured by the #483 review on 3.12.14 against pydicom 3.0.2 with pyjpegls 1.5.1. Two more were stated here, both about a stream of precision 8 or less under BitsAllocated 16, and #454 closed both by widening the decode to the declared container (the entry above). In the first, the read doors returned the 8-bit container where pydicom returns 16 bits, and ingest refused the file. In the second, a precision-8 stream under BitsStored 12 was refused at every door. The value rule this entry set, precision first, is unchanged by #454: the sample 64 in a signed precision-7 stream under BitsStored 8 reads −64, pydicom's value, where it read 64 before this entry. It is now held in `int16`, where it was held in `int8`.
    - **`FF` fill bytes ahead of the SOF55 header** (ITU-T T.81 B.1.1.2). CharLS decodes such a stream, and the segment walk steps over the fill to the frame header's precision. pydicom's header parser reads the `F7 00` after a fill byte as a segment length, finds no precision, and falls back to BitsStored. So a signed precision-12 stream behind two fill bytes under BitsStored 16 reads 2048 there and −2048 here. Isocenter's answer is the frame header's precision, the one CharLS decoded by.
  - **Unchanged.** JPEG 2000: `jpeg2k_decode` already returns signed, sign-extended samples, so *this* rule is keyed on the syntax and never reaches it. It has a rule of its own, keyed on the codestream's SIZ header rather than on BitsStored -- the clause this entry first carried, that an unsigned J2K codestream under PixelRepresentation 1 "is still refused", was superseded by #460 above, which reads it by the header instead. Unsigned files, which get the codec's array untouched. Export, which encodes only JPEG 2000 and carries signed samples natively: a signed 8-, 12- or 16-bit file ingested through this path exports bit-exact, compressed and raw.

- **BREAKING: `Instance.get_pixel_data()` and `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()` return an 8-bit `YBR_FULL` JPEG-LS file as RGB and relabel it `RGB`, as `ingest()` stores it. A signed 8-bit `YBR_FULL` JPEG-LS file now raises at both read doors (#464).** These are files pydicom cannot decode in the environment this package installs (1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.80 and .81), so they reach the imagecodecs fallback.
  - **Before.** Measured on e184933, pydicom 3.0.2, imagecodecs 2026.8.16, on 3.12 and 3.14t. Since #448 `ingest()` has converted the YBR samples with `convert_color_space` and stored RGB under an `RGB` label. The read doors returned the YBR samples exactly as stored, and the file's label still said `YBR_FULL`. That held for both syntaxes, one and two frames, and all three JPEG-LS interleave modes, so one file had two answers. A signed (PixelRepresentation 1) 8-bit `YBR_FULL` file was refused by `ingest()` in `convert_color_space`'s own words, `Decompression Failed: ValueError: Invalid ndarray.dtype 'int8' for color space conversion, must be 'uint8' or an equivalent`, while both read doors returned `int8` YBR samples.
  - **Now, the owner's ruling: convert and relabel.** The handler converts with the same function, from one table (`imagecodecs_handler.CONVERTS_TO`) that ingest and both read doors all read. It rewrites the dataset's `PhotometricInterpretation` to `RGB` (`imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data(ds)` changes the `ds` it is given). `Instance.get_pixel_data()` rewrites the instance's `0028,0004` to `RGB`. Converting without relabelling would be #372's defect, RGB bytes under a YBR label, at a new door. The instance's relabel fires only when the handler converted, and only when the instance already carries a label that differs. It bumps the instance's revision, because a new label is a change the store should hold. A bare `Instance(file_path=...)` with no label gets no descriptor added. After `ingest()` the label is already `RGB`, so on that path nothing is written. The relabel is for hand-built graphs. It is made under `entities.PIXEL_STATE_LOCK`, and only while the array is still unloaded, so a `set_pixel_data()` that lands during the read keeps its own label. #465, in the same release, keeps the set's pixels too; the relabel is now made in the same hold as the publish, on the publishing branch only.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** A read of an unsigned 8-bit `YBR_FULL` JPEG-LS file returns different bytes (RGB, not YBR), mutates the dataset passed to the handler, and may change a labelled instance's PhotometricInterpretation and revision. A read of a signed 8-bit one, which returned `int8` YBR samples, now raises. From the handler it raises ``RuntimeError: its declared colour space 'YBR_FULL' is signed 8-bit, and the conversion to RGB this handler makes, pydicom's `convert_color_space`, takes unsigned samples only: YBR_FULL's chroma is defined with a +128 offset over unsigned samples, so a signed sample has no conversion``. It raises before any decode, with no `imagecodecs failed to decode` prefix. `Instance.get_pixel_data()` raises `RuntimeError: Failed to decompress pixel data for <file> …` carrying the same words on its `imagecodecs fallback:` line, and `ingest()`'s row now reads `… imagecodecs could not decode it either: its declared colour space 'YBR_FULL' is signed 8-bit, …`. **Why refuse rather than convert:** `convert_color_space` has no `int8` path, and YBR_FULL's chroma is defined by PS3.3 C.7.6.3.1.2 with a +128 offset over unsigned samples, so a signed YBR_FULL layout has no meaning and no conversion to honour. pydicom refuses the same file at both its doors, with pyjpegls and natively.
  - **Unchanged.** 16-bit `YBR_FULL` JPEG-LS. The read doors still return its samples as stored under their own `YBR_FULL` label, which is true of them, and `ingest()` still refuses it naming its depth. Whether it is converted or recorded as a limit is #461, which stays open. JPEG 2000 `YBR_RCT`/`YBR_ICT` and the pydicom arm of `Instance.get_pixel_data()` were left unchanged here; the read-door label they left is #482's, below. Pinned at all three doors, on 3.12 and 3.14t, by `tests/test_ybr_jpegls_read_doors.py`.

- **BREAKING: a read door whose decoder returns RGB from a YBR-labelled file now says `RGB`. `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data()` relabels a JPEG 2000 `YBR_RCT`/`YBR_ICT` dataset, and `Instance.get_pixel_data()` relabels a labelled instance wherever the handler or pydicom converted, so a hand-built graph no longer exports RGB bytes under a YBR label (#482).** No returned array changes at any door; labels, and the revisions that carry them, do.
  - **Before.** Measured on dab0ff2, pydicom 3.0.2, imagecodecs 2026.8.16, on 3.12.14 and 3.14.7t. Two paths returned RGB samples under the file's YBR label, which is #372's shape. *The handler under JPEG 2000.* `jpeg2k_decode` undoes the codestream's colour transform and returns RGB, at 8 and 16 bits. `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data(ds)` returned it with `ds.PhotometricInterpretation` still `YBR_RCT` or `YBR_ICT`. A labelled instance over a 16-bit file kept `YBR_RCT` too; such a file reaches the handler from the Instance door because Pillow, pydicom's only J2K plugin here, refuses 16-bit multi-sample. *The Instance door's pydicom arm.* `ds.pixel_array` returns every 8-bit YBR source pydicom decodes as RGB (`as_rgb=True`) and leaves the dataset's label alone. The RGB answer exists only in the decoder's meta, which `pixel_array` discards. Measured for native `YBR_FULL`, JPEG Baseline `YBR_FULL_422` and 8-bit J2K `YBR_RCT`/`YBR_ICT` through Pillow: a labelled instance kept its YBR label over RGB bytes. *On disk.* Export writes the label the instance holds beside the bytes its read returned. So a hand-built graph over a native 8-bit `YBR_FULL` file exported RGB samples under `YBR_FULL`, compressed and native alike, and pydicom reading the export converted them a second time: a maximum difference of 255 from the source, and 160 for JPEG Baseline `YBR_FULL_422`. A hand-built 16-bit J2K `YBR_RCT` graph exported under `YBR_RCT`, natively too, where the samples went through no colour transform for the label to name. After `ingest()` none of this showed. The label is already `RGB` there (#372, #448), and `_make_lightweight_copy` carries it. Only hand-built labelled `Instance(file_path=...)` graphs and direct handler calls reached these paths.
  - **Now, #464's rule: relabel exactly when the decode converts, never one without the other.** The handler's label-only table, `imagecodecs_handler.DECODER_RELABELS`, sits beside `CONVERTS_TO` and not in it. `convert_color_space` has no `YBR_RCT` conversion, and ingest reads `CONVERTS_TO` too. The table is applied only after the decode succeeds. `test_the_handler_relabels_exactly_the_rows_ingest_relabels_without_converting` holds it to the `io_handlers._FALLBACK_PHOTOMETRICS` rows under `_FALLBACK_DECODER_CONVERTS`. The pydicom arm now decodes through `get_decoder(ts).as_array(ds, **as_pixel_options(ds))`, which is the call `Dataset.pixel_array` makes, and keeps the meta. Where pydicom would refuse before decoding, for a dataset with no Transfer Syntax UID or one it has no decoder for, the arm still asks `ds.pixel_array`, so those refusals keep pydicom's words. Both arms relabel through `Instance._relabel_to_decoded_colour`, under `PIXEL_STATE_LOCK`, only while the array is unloaded, and only when the instance already carries a label. The comparison is with the file's label, so an instance labelled wrongly for some other reason is not this read's to correct. The hand-built export now writes `RGB` over RGB samples, the same label and stored samples the ingested export writes for the same file.
  - **What a previously-working call now does differently.** `imagecodecs_handler.get_pixel_data(ds)` on a JPEG 2000 `YBR_RCT`/`YBR_ICT` dataset sets `ds.PhotometricInterpretation` to `RGB`. `Instance.get_pixel_data()` on a labelled instance over such a file, or over any 8-bit YBR file pydicom decodes, changes the instance's `0028,0004` to `RGB` and advances its revision, so the next `save()` writes the label. An export of such a hand-built graph writes the instance's `RGB` where it wrote the YBR label. **For a compressed export that label is no longer the one on disk:** #490, in Fixed below, settled the question this entry left open and the exporter now declares `YBR_RCT` for the multiple-component transform its own codestream carries. So a compressed export of a J2K `YBR_RCT` source writes `YBR_RCT` again -- not the source file's label passed through, which is what this entry fixed, but the label the exporter's own encode earns. An uncompressed export writes `RGB`. **Which object keeps the new label depends on the strategy, as it has since #464.** `session.export()` always runs its workers in processes (#185), so the relabel is made on the worker's copy: the exported file says `RGB`, and the instance in the caller's graph keeps its old label until its own next read. `DicomExporter.write_tree()` under threads, the free-threaded default, relabels the live instance and advances its revision there and then. `redact()` is not like `export()` here: under processes it now brings the label back with its result (below), so after `redact()` the caller's graph says `RGB` too. Two tests mocked `Dataset.pixel_array` on a `MagicMock` dataset: `test_compression_deps.py` and `test_entities.py::test_lazy_loading`. They now mock `isocenter.entities.get_decoder` instead, and their assertions are unchanged.
  - **And `redact()` under processes, where the defect predates this entry.** *Before.* On a GIL build `Session.redact()` runs its workers in processes. The worker's read relabelled its own copy, but the result it sent back carried `0008,0008`, `0028,0301`, `0008,2111`, the redaction hash and the new SOP Instance UID (#228), and not `0028,0004`. So the caller's instance kept `YBR_FULL`/`YBR_RCT` over the worker's RGB frame, with `file_path` cleared and no file left to read again, and `export()` wrote that label beside RGB samples. pydicom read a native `YBR_FULL` export back up to 116 from the source, and `verify_readback` said nothing. #493's review measured it on 168fdd6, and it was measured again on this branch before the fix, on 3.12.14 and on 3.14.7t with processes forced, native and compressed. *Now.* The worker's label travels on the result as `photometric_interpretation`, and `Session._apply_redaction_outcomes` assigns it beside the loader rebind, under the same `PIXEL_STATE_LOCK`, and only when the result carries a loader. The `mark_modified()` already there moves the revision. *Unchanged.* Under threads, and on the serial `RedactionService.redact_machine_instances`, the instance that reads is the caller's own, and its read relabels it. Both were already right, and are pinned beside the fixed arm by `test_a_redacted_hand_built_graph_exports_rgb_bytes_under_an_rgb_label`, forced each way on 3.12 and 3.14t.
  - **Unchanged.** Every returned array, at every door. Ingested graphs. 16-bit `YBR_FULL` JPEG-LS, which is #461's. Pinned by `tests/test_ybr_read_door_labels.py` on 3.12 and 3.14t, including the export-to-disk scenario, compressed and native.

- **BREAKING (processes only): a `PhiFinding` returned by `Session.scan_pixel_content()` now names the live `Instance` in `session.store`, not a copy unpickled from the worker (#412).** Under processes (the default on GIL builds, and wherever `ISOCENTER_FORCE_PROCESSES=1` or `ISOCENTER_MAX_TASKS_PER_CHILD` is set), `finding.entity` was the worker's copy: `finding.entity is <the instance in session.store>` was `False`, an edit through it reached neither the graph nor the export, and the copy carried the frame the worker had decoded for OCR, resident in `pixel_array`. Under threads (the free-threaded default) it was already the live object. It is now the live instance under both, resolved by `_rehydrate_findings` (the path `audit()` has always used), or `None` when the instance cannot be found in the graph. `docs/api/stability.md` now states that meaning for the findings of both `audit()` and `scan_pixel_content()`. One limit it states with it: rehydration is keyed on the SOP Instance UID, so findings on a UID that more than one instance carries all resolve to one of those instances, the last in graph order. Since #431 `ingest()` cannot produce such a graph; only a graph built or edited by hand can carry one.

  What a previously-working call now does differently, on the processes path, which is the default on GIL builds: `finding.entity.pixel_array` is `None` where it used to be the decoded frame, so `finding.entity.pixel_array.shape` now raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'` (`finding.entity.get_pixel_data()` loads the frame). And an edit made through `finding.entity`, which used to be a no-op on a copy nobody kept, now changes the live graph and therefore the export.

  The old behaviour was wrong because `PhiFinding.entity` is frozen at 1.0 yet meant two different things depending on which strategy `run_parallel()` resolved, and a caller can change that without editing a line, through an environment variable or the interpreter build. It was also expensive: `_verify_worker` returned `RedactionVerifier.verify_instance()`'s findings with the instance attached, and OCR had just decoded the frame onto that instance, so the worker's result carried the decoded frame back to the parent. That is once per scanned instance that raised a finding, however many findings it raised -- pickle memoises the shared instance within one result, so a second finding on the same frame costs about 150 bytes, not a second frame -- and it undid the lazy sidecar load. Measured under real tesseract 5.5.3 with pytesseract 0.3.13, locally and not in CI, on one 256×256 16-bit frame reading `JOHN DOE` behind a sidecar-style loader: a result carrying one finding pickled to 132372 bytes and the two-finding result to 132519 on 3.12.14 (132348 and 132495 on 3.14.7t); the same two-finding result is 542 bytes with this change, on both. The worker now drops the reference, as `scan_worker` does. `RedactionVerifier.verify_instance()` still attaches the instance it is given, so a direct caller of that tier-2 method sees no change. `auto_remediate_config()` reads only each finding's `metadata` and `value` and is unaffected. `tests/test_scan_pixel_findings_name_the_live_graph.py` pins the identity under both strategies, with each finding stamped by the pid of the process that scanned it so the processes case cannot pass by running in threads; T-394a in `tests/test_scan_pixel_content_dispatches_its_worker.py` pins the strip, which the identity test cannot see because rehydration overwrites the copy either way.

- **A descriptor edit made while the pixels are unloaded now changes how the stored pixels are read, in the live session as in a reopened one (#417).** `SidecarPixelLoader` captured Rows, Columns, SamplesPerPixel, NumberOfFrames, BitsAllocated, PixelRepresentation and the `_ISOCENTER_PIXEL_DTYPE` float carrier once, when it was built, and every later `get_pixel_data()` and `export()` in the session read the stored bytes under those captured values. So `set_attr("0028,0103", 1)` (PixelRepresentation) on an unloaded instance still returned `uint16`; a Rows/Columns edit from 4x4 to 2x8 still returned `(4, 4)`, and `export()` wrote Rows 4 and Columns 4 back out, silently reverting the edit; and an edit the bytes cannot satisfy exported as though it had not been made. The same store, reopened, honoured each edit or refused it, because a reopened session builds its loader from the attributes as they now are, so the live session and the reopened one disagreed about the same bytes. A save between the edit and the read changed nothing: the capture was stale from the `set_attr` on. The issue's own premise, that the *exported file* carried a container that did not match its bytes, is not what was measured. Every exported file was internally consistent and decodable, because the writer takes geometry from the array's shape and BitsAllocated from its itemsize; it was consistent with the old descriptors and wrong about the edit. `get_pixel_data()` now compares the loader's capture with the instance on every read (`SidecarPixelLoader.describes`) and, when they differ, reads the same stored, hash-checked bytes through a loader built from the instance as it is now (`for_instance`, which copies the old loader's hash verbatim, `None` included). The rebuilt loader is used for that read and not stored back on the instance: a read that wrote `_pixel_loader` outside `_pixel_swap_lock` could publish a stale loader over the one `_apply_redaction_outcomes` had just bound to a redacted frame (#274).

  **What breaks:** code that relied on the old values surviving an edit now gets the new reading. An edit the stored bytes cannot satisfy (BitsAllocated 16→8, or Rows×Columns smaller than the stored samples) now raises `RuntimeError("Pixel Loader failed for <uid>: Integrity Error: frame for <uid> holds N samples; geometry (...) needs M ...")` from `get_pixel_data()`, and `export()` records an `ERROR` row for that instance and raises `ExportError` when nothing else was delivered. A reopened session already gave that refusal. Since #434, `discard_pixel_data()` puts back the descriptors `set_pixel_data()` wrote, so a discard no longer changes how the stored bytes are read; a descriptor edit made after a discard is read under the edited descriptors before and after a save, like any other edit. Filtering the check on `_pixel_array_unwritten` was measured and rejected: it kept the old reading for one read only, then flipped with no save between.

- **BREAKING: `Instance.discard_pixel_data()` undoes the whole `set_pixel_data()` it discards, the pixels and the descriptors it wrote (#434).** A frozen method's effect on `attributes`, and so on the next read, changes.
  - **Before.** Measured on c9e9938, on an ingested 4x4 `uint16` instance:
    - `set_pixel_data(arr.view(np.int16))` → `discard_pixel_data()` → `get_pixel_data()` returned `int16 [-25536, …]`, live and after a save and a reopen.
    - `set_pixel_data(np.full((8, 8), 7, np.uint8))` → `discard_pixel_data()` left Rows 8, Columns 8 and BitsAllocated 8 over the stored 4x4 16-bit frame. So `get_pixel_data()` raised `RuntimeError: Pixel Loader failed for <uid>: Integrity Error: frame for <uid> …`, `export()` raised `ExportError: … wrote 0 of 1 planned instances`, and the next `save()` wrote those descriptors to the store, so the reopened session raised too.
    - A three-frame array, a `float32` array and a colour array did the same, through NumberOfFrames, the `_ISOCENTER_PIXEL_DTYPE` carrier, and SamplesPerPixel/PhotometricInterpretation/PlanarConfiguration respectively.
  - **Now.**
    - `set_pixel_data()` records the prior value, or absence, of each descriptor it can write: Rows, Columns, SamplesPerPixel, NumberOfFrames, PhotometricInterpretation, PlanarConfiguration, BitsAllocated, PixelRepresentation and the float/bool dtype carrier.
    - `discard_pixel_data()` puts them back when it drops the array, so those calls read the stored `uint16` frame, and export and reopen it. A tag the set introduced is deleted, not zeroed.
    - A second `set_pixel_data()` before the discard keeps the first record.
    - Once the replacement is written, whether by a save or the redaction swap, it is the stored frame, and a discard drops the array and keeps the descriptors that describe it. The processes-path redaction rebind drops the record too, since its loader reads the redacted frame.
    - A refused discard (no loader and no file) keeps both the array and its descriptors.
    - The instance stays dirty after a set and a discard, as before.
